body:
Logging soreness against the wrong day left no way to correct it from the view that showed the mistake: the journal list held the only edit affordance (the wrench beside the date), while Lanes and Timeline drew the same entries with hover detail only. Since #81 made Lanes the landing view, the default page had no way into the editor at all.

An entry is identified by `(date, sourceWorkoutId)` and both views already hold that pair for every cell they draw, so each now hands off to the same editor: a logged day in a lane stripe, and a filled cell in a recovery curve. Unlogged days stay inert — there is nothing to edit.

The second commit is unrelated to the feature and can be read separately. Running this repo under `devctl` had never actually worked: it requires a managed frontend to prove its identity on `/__devctl/health` and probes over IPv4 loopback, while Vite's default host resolves verbatim to `::1` alone on Windows. Every launch ended as a failed start that left an orphaned Vite behind. The frontend now serves that endpoint (serve-only, inert unless `DEVCTL_MANAGED=1`, so it cannot reach a production build) and binds `127.0.0.1`. Its one visible consequence: headless Chrome does not fall back from `::1`, so the screenshot recipe in CLAUDE.md now uses the literal address — against `localhost` it fails silently with no PNG.

Needs a matching `kill-me-frontend` entry in `devctl-apps.json` (shell-config-profile-5) to launch; `-Cwd` alone cannot borrow the chess-tactics entry, whose project name and backend health path both fail the identity check.

## Verification

Against live data on the dev server, signed in as admin:

- Lanes loads as the active view; clicking the Aug 22 stripe opens the editor for D06 Bicep / Biceps 8, with Date and Delete entry.
- Timeline's filled cells open the same editor for their own date.
- `devctl up kill-me-frontend` reports ready with all seven identity checks passing.
- Mobile render of `/soreness` at 390px is unchanged.
- `npm run build` and `eslint` clean (two pre-existing exhaustive-deps warnings).
title: Make a logged soreness day clickable wherever it is drawn
